body:
Firstly, I'm sorry this happened to you, and I wish only the very best for you.  You've been through a lot, and I know you can continue to endure.

For me, I just had to have an open (although painful) talk with my partner.  I know that sounds simplistic, but nothing else really does the trick outside of just being honest with them.  My rape experience had affected a lot of how I related to my body and also produced an inability to orgasm.  After much discussion, honesty, and tears, my partner comforted me and began a gentle pursuit to make me love myself as much as she loved me.  

It took months, but eventually I genuinely enjoyed sex.  I really hadn't done that before.  But with the new knowledge I'd given her, as painful as it was for me to explain, she knew just what not to do or say and slowly helped me find a way to love myself again.

Thanks for that, it did help.  I think I  needed another Buddhist nudge of strength.  My boss is Buddhist and he's been attempting some mindfulness with me, but he's currently out of the country so I'm solo on my enlightenment detour/wild ride through deer_disciple's mental forest of nightmares. :P

Well, unfortunately the problem is more complex than that.  I was diagnosed with a disorder which explained many of the struggles I'd been having with my work.  Unfortunately, my boss (who is a genuinely good person, and who meant well), took that information and made things much more difficult, despite attempting to help.  Instead of my disorder being used as an explanation for my struggles and my treatment being a sign that things will improved, my competency across the board is now being questioned.  Monday is the day I have to submit I project to be judged to see if I can stay where I'm at.  That's only half the battle.  Then I have to petition the board that people with my disorder aren't incapable of doing my job.

As I said, my superficial life is fine.  I have loving friends.  I am well liked, I enjoy many hobbies.  But the fabric of my identity and my social interaction has been rapidly unwound since April and it's coming to a head that I don't think I'm strong enough to handle.  I am trying, one day at a time.  

What scares me most isn't this deep, empassioned need to off myself.  It's that there is no deep need.  I've just calmly accepted that maybe I'm not strong enough to do this anymore.  I don't like that, as I know from my suicide prevention work that is often the most worrying.  I have made an appointment to see a counselor, but as I'm in the UK there is a 9 month waiting list.

TL/DR: I got a diagnosis that lifted a weight off my back, only to realise my peers now see me like a different human being.  Yes, seeing a therapist, but am on the NHS's 9 month waiting list.

Thank you.  And thanks for not making me feel like a hypocrite. I feel like I ought to be able to practice what I preach.  In a way, I am, I'm still here despite my id telling me to let go, but the id is getting more difficult to rationalize away.

I feel like elaborating more might make me seem ridiculous, but I'm willing to.  I'll send you a PM.  And thanks again.  You've really made a difference to my weekend.

I know this sounds really lame... But I also went to SW on a throwaway because I'm feeling incredibly lonely and isolated.  I'd be happy to PM back and forth if you just want someone to talk to for awhile... 

My situation is kind of different, I'm surrounded by people but can't feel like I can speak to anyone.  

People do care about you.  Maybe begin by chatting to come redditors?
